- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.3) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model under-forecasts; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing downside.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 3–5 days after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction, not just magnitude.
